--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.layout_arf()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Place the nodes with the attractive and repulsive forces (ARF) layout. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.layout_arf()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Place the nodes with the attractive and repulsive forces (ARF) layout. title: >- [Graph.layout_arf()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Place the nodes with the attractive and repulsive forces (ARF) layout. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Place the nodes with the attractive and repulsive forces (ARF) layout. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7403-L7548){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.layout_arf( scaling=1.0, a=1.1, etol=1e-06, dt=0.001, max_iter=1000, initial=None, scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![ARF layout](../assets/graphs/layout-arf.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, a barbell graph scattered at random: two triangles, nodes 1 to 3 and 5 to 7, joined through node 4. On the right, layout_arf(seed=19) pulls joined nodes together and pushes every pair apart, so the two triangles sit apart with node 4 bridging them." width="100%"} ARF (Geipel, 2007) joins every pair of nodes by a weak spring of strength `1`, strengthened to `a=` for adjacent pairs, and lets every pair repel with force `rho / d`, where `rho = scaling * sqrt(n)`. The springs on all pairs hold the layout together in a round, evenly filled disc, avoiding the large gaps a spring layout can leave, while the stronger springs on edges pull connected groups together. Positions follow the force field in small time steps `dt=` until the summed force falls to `etol=` or `max_iter=` steps have run. The result is centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. This follows NetworkX's `arf_layout()` with two differences: edges strengthen the spring between their ends in both directions (NetworkX strengthens only the `source -> target` entry of the spring matrix, so directed graphs get lopsided forces), and the result is rescaled (NetworkX returns raw coordinates). Each step costs `O(n^2)`. Edge weights are not used. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [scaling]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Strength of the repulsion, which sets the size of the disc. Default is `1.0`. [a]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Spring strength between adjacent nodes; must be greater than `1`. Larger values separate clusters more clearly. Default is `1.1`. [etol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stop once the summed force on all nodes falls to this. Default is `1e-6`. [dt]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.001]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Time step of the simulation. Default is `1e-3`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of steps. Default is `1000`. [initial]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Union[str, dict]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Starting positions, as the name of a node attribute holding `(x, y)` pairs or a dict mapping node IDs or labels to pairs. Nodes without one start at random. If `None` (default), all nodes start at random in the unit square. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. `None` keeps the raw coordinates (`center=` is then ignored). Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random starting positions. If `None` (default), the layout differs on every call. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `a=` is not greater than `1`, `scaling=` or `dt=` is not positive, `etol=` is negative, an initial position is not a pair of finite numbers, or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~layout_spring`) : Place nodes with a force-directed spring model. [](`~layout_forceatlas2`) : Place nodes with the ForceAtlas2 model. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The attractive and repulsive forces layout (ARF) joins every pair of nodes with a spring, and `a=` sets how much stronger the springs along edges are than the others. ### Tight and loose cliques A barbell graph is two cliques of 6 joined by a path of 3. With the default `a=1.1` on the left, the cliques spread out. With `a=3` on the right, each clique pulls tight and the path between them stands out: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#cd26dd32 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec barbell = ec.Graph().add_barbell_graph(6, 3) barbell.layout_arf(seed=5).plot( layout="pos", width=320, height=320, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#8e39001f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} barbell.layout_arf(a=3, seed=5).plot( layout="pos", width=320, height=320, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: The result depends on `seed=`. [Layouts](../user-guide/layouts.qmd#force-directed-layouts) compares the four force-directed layouts on the dolphin network.
